seoTitle: Tangier cruise port guide: medina, Kasbah and Hercules
seoDescription: Tanger Ville berth is about 800 m from the centre, 15–20 min on foot. American Legation 50 MAD, Caves of Hercules 30 MAD (2026). Back aboard 60 min early.
quickAnswer: Cruise ships berth at Tanger Ville, the city port at the foot of the medina, about 800 m from the centre; a few ships tender. You can walk into the medina in 15–20 minutes, uphill, or take the port shuttle or the hop-on bus that stops outside the port gate. Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard, 90 if your ship is tendering.
intro: Tangier is one of the few Moroccan ports where the old town starts at the port gate. The medina climbs the hill directly behind the harbour to the Kasbah, with views across the Strait of Gibraltar to Spain. The city port was converted from cargo to passengers and leisure in the 2010s, and cruise calls are growing fast: 153 in 2025, with 185 expected in 2026. The main challenge for independent visitors is not distance but persistence: unofficial guides wait near the port and in the medina. Walk with purpose, use an offline map, and the day is easy to manage on your own.
tenderNotes: Most ships berth alongside at the cruise quay. Ships are sometimes tendered instead; if yours is, add time for the tender queue on the way back.

terminals.name: Tanger Ville cruise terminal
terminals.notes: Passenger terminal shared with ferries, in the bay below the medina and run by the Société de Gestion du Port de Tanger Ville (SGPTV). Shuttle buses and taxis wait at the terminal. A new telescopic gangway system is due in 2027.

walkability.detail: About 15–20 minutes on foot to the city centre. The medina rises directly from the port area, so the walk is uphill on steep, cobbled lanes. To avoid the climb, ride the hop-on bus up to Place du 9 Avril (Stop 2) and walk down through the medina.

transportSections.detail: Walk out of the port and into the lower medina. The streets are steep and cobbled; the harbour is visible from most of the medina, which helps if you get lost.
Runs from the terminal. Check the drop-off point and last return time on board.
Stops just outside the port gate. The blue route reaches Stop 2, Place du 9 Avril, from where you can walk downhill through the medina back to the port.

Taxis wait at the terminal. Agree the price, the stops and the return time before you set off. Petit taxis serve the city; for the Caves of Hercules and Cape Spartel you need a grand taxi or an hourly hire.

transportSections.mode: Grand taxi to the Caves of Hercules and Cape Spartel
transportSections.detail: The caves are about 14–20 km west of the city on the Atlantic coast; Cape Spartel lighthouse is about 5 km from the caves. Agree a return fare including waiting time.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard, or 90 minutes if your ship is tendering. From the Kasbah or Café Hafa, start walking down at least 90 minutes before all-aboard; from the Caves of Hercules, leave at least 2 hours before.
returnTiming.detail: The walk down to the port is quicker than the walk up, but the medina is a maze and touts can slow you down. Keep the harbour in view and head downhill. The coast road to the caves is about 40 minutes each way.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a petit taxi to the port (Port Tanger Ville). If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme.

excursionAdvice: Tangier is easy to do on your own: the medina starts at the port and the main sights are within walking distance. A ship tour or an official guide is worth it if you do not want to deal with touts, who are persistent here; a badge-carrying guide keeps them away. Take the ship's excursion for Chefchaouen, Tetouan or Asilah, which are outside the city and too far for a relaxed independent return.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00, all-aboard is 17:30 and the day is not a Tuesday (when the Kasbah museums close).

steps.what: Walk off the ship and through the port into the lower medina. Decline offers from unofficial guides politely and keep walking.
Climb through the medina to the Kasbah, at the top of the hill, for the view over the Strait.
Kasbah Museum of Mediterranean Cultures in the old sultan's palace, Dar el Makhzen (closed Tuesdays).
Walk to Café Hafa for mint tea on its terraces above the Strait of Gibraltar.
Down through the medina to the American Legation Museum (50 MAD).
Lunch at Restaurant Bachir, off Avenue Pasteur in the new town.
Grand Socco and the Mendoubia Gardens; coffee at the Cinémathèque café at Cinema Rif.
Walk downhill through the medina to the port, keeping the harbour in view.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard (16:00 if you are tendering).

sights.name: The medina
sights.why: The walled old town climbing from the port to the Kasbah: souks, the Petit Socco cafés and narrow residential lanes.
sights.tip: The harbour is visible from almost everywhere; head downhill to get back to the port.

sights.name: Kasbah and Kasbah Museum of Mediterranean Cultures
sights.why: The fortified top of the medina, with the former sultan's palace (Dar el Makhzen) and its museum of regional history and Andalusian garden.
sights.cost: Kasbah free; museum ticket covers the neighbouring contemporary art space
sights.tip: The museums here close on Tuesdays.

sights.name: Tangier American Legation Museum
sights.why: Described as the only US National Historic Landmark outside the United States, with a Paul Bowles wing and art collections, inside the medina.
sights.cost: 50 MAD for visitors not resident in Morocco (2026)
sights.tip: Open Monday to Friday 10:00–17:00 and weekends 10:00–15:00; closed on Moroccan public holidays.

sights.name: Café Hafa
sights.why: A terraced tea house of nearly a century, up the Kasbah hill, looking over the Strait to Spain.
sights.tip: Ask for mint tea without sugar if you prefer it that way; it comes very sweet.

sights.name: Grand Socco and the Mendoubia Gardens
sights.why: The main square where the new town meets the medina, with gardens next to it that hold a huge old banyan tree.
sights.tip: Stop for coffee at the Cinémathèque café on the square.

sights.name: Dar Niaba Museum
sights.why: A 19th-century building that was Morocco's first foreign affairs office, now a museum of diplomacy.
sights.tip: Closed Tuesdays; in the middle of the medina.

sights.name: Caves of Hercules
sights.why: Sea caves on the Atlantic coast west of the city; they flood at high tide.
sights.cost: 30 MAD entry (2026), plus a grand taxi
sights.tip: Combine with the Cape Spartel lighthouse, about 5 km away. Leave the caves at least 2 hours before all-aboard.

sights.name: Cape Spartel
sights.why: A headland at the entrance to the Strait of Gibraltar, marked by a 19th-century lighthouse.
sights.tip: Only worth it combined with the caves.

beaches.name: Atlantic coast by the Caves of Hercules
beaches.note: Strong currents and unexpected waves; many Moroccan beaches have little or no lifeguard cover. Treat it as a walk, not a swim, unless conditions are clearly calm.

food.dish: Mint tea and bissara (fava bean soup)
Kefta or shrimp tagine, fried calamari; couscous on Fridays
Rghifa (savoury flatbread) with cheese and egg, fresh juice
Coffee and juice with a local crowd

commonMistakes.mistake: Letting an unofficial guide attach himself to you at the port.
commonMistakes.fix: Say no firmly and keep walking. If you want a guide, hire an official one with a badge, or book through the ship.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning the Kasbah museums for a Tuesday.
commonMistakes.fix: Most Tangier museums close on Tuesdays; the American Legation stays open.

commonMistakes.mistake: Walking up the medina in the midday heat.
commonMistakes.fix: Climb to the Kasbah first thing, or take the hop-on bus up to Place du 9 Avril and walk down.

commonMistakes.mistake: Taking a taxi to the caves without agreeing the return.
commonMistakes.fix: Agree the fare, the waiting time and the return in advance.
Carry small dirham notes; some vendors claim to have no change.

safety: Tangier is busy but manageable. The main nuisance is persistent touts and people posing as guides, especially near the port and in the medina. Petty theft is common in medinas and on beaches, including pickpocketing and bag-snatching, so keep valuables out of sight. The medina lanes are steep, cobbled and slippery after rain. Avoid quiet lanes after dark. Women may receive unwanted attention; loose clothing that covers arms and legs helps. On the Atlantic coast the currents are strong.
scams: Unofficial guides who meet passengers near the port and follow them through the medina, then demand payment. Official guides carry a badge.
Short-changing: some vendors and ticket desks claim to have no change. Carry small notes.
Taxi fares that change at the end of the trip. Agree the price first.
Goods swapped for inferior ones after purchase, and card fraud. Watch your card and check items before they are wrapped.
accessibility: The berth is alongside, so there is no tender transfer on most calls. The medina is steep, cobbled and stepped in places, which makes it hard going for wheelchairs and anyone with limited mobility. The new town around Avenue Pasteur is flatter. A taxi or the hop-on bus can take you up to Place du 9 Avril, which avoids the climb from the port. Ask the ship whether the shuttle is accessible.
rainyDay: Visit the museums: the American Legation, Dar Niaba and the Kasbah Museum (all except the Legation closed on Tuesdays). Take long café stops at Café Hafa or in the new town. The cobbled lanes are slippery in rain; wear shoes with grip.
crowdTips: Cruise calls are rising, and ships of 3,000–4,000 passengers are common. Tour groups move through the medina and Kasbah from mid-morning, so go up to the Kasbah first. Walking away from the groups also reduces the attention from touts.

faqs.q: Is Tangier walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre is about 800 m away, 15–20 minutes on foot, but the medina is uphill on steep cobbles.
Usually not. Ships normally berth at Tanger Ville, but some calls are tendered.

faqs.q: How do I get from Tangier cruise port to the medina?
faqs.a: Walk straight in from the port. To avoid the climb, take the hop-on bus to Place du 9 Avril and walk down.

faqs.q: What can I do in Tangier in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Kasbah and its museum, tea at Café Hafa, the medina and the American Legation, then the Grand Socco.

faqs.q: How do I get to the Caves of Hercules from Tangier cruise port?
faqs.a: By grand taxi or an hourly taxi, about 40 minutes each way. Entry is 30 MAD (2026). Combine with Cape Spartel.

faqs.q: Are there beaches near Tangier cruise port?
faqs.a: The Atlantic coast near the Caves of Hercules, about 40 minutes by taxi, but currents are strong and lifeguards are often absent.

faqs.q: Is Tangier safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Expect persistent touts, watch for pickpockets and agree taxi fares first.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide in Tangier?
faqs.a: No, but an official guide with a badge keeps touts away. Avoid people who offer to guide you at the port.
